decision.candidate: dead-write-only exact product capture with one synchronous 1152-bit single-port 1RW read-XOR-write scratch
decision.reason: Dead-write-only and combined PVRF have identical frozen cycles; combined saves only 244346 additional one-block writes. The minimal realizable point must preserve the M505 two-reserved-entry schedule while replacing the open concurrent-1R1W scratch with nine generated 128x128-bit 1RW macros.

included: Exact dynamic 64-row subset matcher with M504 cleanroom tie semantics
Ping-pong 64x32-bit row directory and two 64-bit parent-live bitmaps
Stable popcount-then-row-id ordered scheduler with one earliest-parent lookahead
Deadline-hold single-port arbiter, one-cycle response tracking, and two-reserved-entry ordered parent response queue
M474 signed12 reconstruction and signed19 psum arithmetic
Nine-slice 128x128-bit generated 1RW SRAM wrapper using rows 0 through 63
Architectural psum commit boundary and exact completion counters
excluded: Any second structural retry if this implementation misses a hard gate

reuse_matrix.reuse: Signed12 row reconstruction, signed19 psum update, overflow checks, synchronous-read direct-response mux, same-address final-result forwarding concept
reuse_matrix.must_change: Scratch port and completion coupling; M474 assumes separate read and write ports and sets row_complete equal to scratch write

reuse_matrix.reuse: Two-reserved-entry FIFO ordering, no same-cycle consume credit, pop-response-forward enqueue order, stale same-address backpressure guard
reuse_matrix.must_change: Queue data path must be sliced physically; existing packed dual-slot implementation is not an admitted physical block

reuse_matrix.reuse: Functional queue next-state, arithmetic lane partition, targeted and full regression intent
reuse_matrix.must_change: Do not reuse the failed explicit BUFFD tree as physical evidence; the mapped M498 line lost the required topology and failed fanout, capacitance, and transition gates

reuse_matrix.reuse: 3 ns TSMC28 constraint/report methodology and arithmetic logic reference
reuse_matrix.must_change: The 37316.285232 um2 zero-macro result excludes matcher, scheduler, response queue, parent macros, and psum memory and is not a total-area result

reuse_matrix.reuse: Active-low CEB/WEB pin convention and coherent parallel-slice binding pattern
reuse_matrix.must_change: Instantiate nine, not four, slices; address width is seven while legal task rows require A[6]=0

scratch_protocol.control: All nine macros share CLK, CEB, WEB, and A; each macro carries one contiguous 128-bit slice
scratch_protocol.read: enable=1, write_enable=0 at wrapper level; CEB=0, WEB=1 at macro pins
scratch_protocol.write: enable=1, write_enable=1 at wrapper level; CEB=0, WEB=0 at macro pins
scratch_protocol.hard_rule: scratch_read_enable XOR scratch_write_enable; never both in one cycle
scratch_protocol.response: A read accepted at edge N produces the parent word for edge N+1; response identity is registered with the request
scratch_protocol.same_address: A live final write plus same-address parent request performs the write, suppresses the macro read, and enqueues the just-computed value
scratch_protocol.capacity: 18432 physical bytes and 78825.2454 um2 for the nine generated macro instances before placement/routing

metadata_and_schedule.matcher_semantics: For each active current 16-bit mask with population at least two, select the subset candidate with maximum population; exclude equal-pattern candidates at the same or later row ID; ties preserve the lowest eligible row ID. Residual is current XOR parent.
metadata_and_schedule.directory_entry: 32 bits per row: residual mask 16, parent ID 6, parent-valid 1, original population 5, four reserved/protocol bits; row ID is the address
metadata_and_schedule.directory_banking: Two 64-entry banks are mandatory because M528 overlaps next-task preprocess with current-task work
metadata_and_schedule.live_generation: Clear the inactive 64-bit bitmap at task acquisition and set live[parent_id] for every accepted parent descriptor. Execution may start only after matcher completion and bank handoff.
metadata_and_schedule.live_storage: Two 64-bit bitmaps, one per ping-pong directory bank. Dead/live is one bit; no refcount class is stored.
metadata_and_schedule.written_storage: One 64-bit written bitmap per executing bank, cleared at bank activation and set only by an accepted live parent-scratch write
metadata_and_schedule.ordering: Active rows issue in stable lexicographic order (population(original), row_id). Parent requests remain in consumer order.
metadata_and_schedule.lookahead: At most the earliest unserved parent edge is exposed. Its consumer position is retained so deadline hold is legal only for the immediately next active row.
metadata_and_schedule.deadline_hold: If a live current row would finish and write while a ready different parent for the immediately next active row needs the single port, suppress current issue for one cycle, accept the read, then finish/write when the response is pending.
metadata_and_schedule.dead_final: A dead current row suppresses only parent-scratch write. It still performs the arithmetic final beat, psum write, row_complete, and architectural completion; the free scratch port may accept a legal read.
metadata_and_schedule.live_final: Every live row writes, including single-use rows already forwarded. This is the dead-write-only contract and prevents accidental combined-PVRF drift.

known_missing_blocks: A dynamic 64-candidate subset CAM/tournament implementing the exact M504 parent tie rule; M348/M363 are static Hamming matchers and cannot be instantiated as-is
The 17-population stable row-order scanner and earliest-parent lookahead scheduler
The ping-pong row directory, live bitmap ownership/epoch protocol, and written bitmap
A nine-macro 1152-bit 1RW adapter with vendor-view VCS binding and macro-DB DC binding
A physically clean two-entry 1152-bit response queue. M477/M498 prove the semantics but not a clean implementation
A matched strong-zero/bit total-area wrapper and complete resident-psum port contract
Integrated SAIF, macro, DRAM, and total energy accounting

assertions: Never assert scratch read and scratch write together; all nine macro slices see identical control and address
Dead final acceptance implies no scratch write but exactly one psum commit and row completion
Live final acceptance implies exactly one scratch write even for a single-use forwarded row
Forward implies a live accepted final beat, equal address, no macro read, and new-value data
A stalled same-address final request under psum backpressure cannot read stale data
Read response is exactly one cycle and preserves request ID; no read occurs before written[parent] unless the same-cycle forward supplies it
Reserved queue occupancy including pending response never exceeds two and same-cycle consume does not create prefetch credit
FIFO parent IDs and data match consumer order; task completion leaves no pending response or queued parent
Directory/live bank cannot be overwritten before release; execution cannot observe a partially generated live bitmap
Every parent descriptor addresses a live row and every dead row has exact parent refcount zero in the reference scoreboard
Stable issue/prefetch/psum payload under backpressure, sticky protocol fault, and atomic overflow block
Issue count, parent edges, dead elisions, macro reads/writes, holds, stalls, psum commits, and row completions match the M528 reference counters
covers: dead final plus concurrent different-parent macro read
live final deadline hold, read acceptance, next-cycle write, and response enqueue
same-address live forward with macro read suppressed
pending read response plus forward dual enqueue
queue full consume with no same-cycle prefetch credit
three or more consecutive dead completions and alternating dead/live completions
exact-parent and partial-parent rows, multi-beat rows, and back-to-back architectural completions
psum sink stall on a same-address request and release to new-value forward
ping-pong matcher/executor overlap and bank handoff at task boundary
row IDs 0 and 63 and nonzero activity in every one of the nine 128-bit macro slices
wrong parent ID, read-before-write, dirty reserved bits, overflow, stale epoch, and illegal dead-parent attacks

physical_hard_gates.precondition: The sealed M528 same-ledger CPU recompute and an independent result hammer must pass before any RTL authoring or EDA run
physical_hard_gates.vcs: Directed plus randomized VCS/SVA and frozen trace recurrence; zero numeric, ordering, protocol, counter, and cycle mismatch. Aggregate recurrence must remain within 1 percent of 435293339 cycles and retain at least 1.50x versus 760350133 and 757946784.
physical_hard_gates.dc_sta: Exactly nine generated SRAM macros, no inferred parent-scratch registers, total capacity at most 245760 bytes, 3.000 ns setup and hold nonnegative, zero max-capacitance/max-transition/max-fanout violations, zero unconstrained paths/latches/multiple drivers, and macro plus interconnect delays included.
physical_hard_gates.area_efficiency: Matched local throughput per total area, including matcher, scheduler, directory, live/written metadata, response queue, nine macros, adapters, and matched resident-psum boundary, must be at least 1.10x versus the strongest matched zero/bit wrapper.
physical_hard_gates.formality: RTL-to-mapped-netlist Formality passes with nine SRAM cells as matched black boxes/cutpoints; a separate invariant miter proves dead-write-only and all-write architectural psum/row outputs equivalent when the generated live bitmap is exact.
physical_hard_gates.ptpx_energy: SAIF/PTPX logic energy plus generated-macro read/write/leakage and DRAM energy must show at least 20 percent four-Conv energy reduction or at least 1.25x EDP improvement. Keep 9069207552 weight-DRAM bytes and 30457108224 all-eight-block logical parent-scratch bytes visible.
physical_hard_gates.failure: Any failed identity, cycle, capacity, DRC, timing, Formality, area-efficiency, or energy/EDP gate permanently closes this one RTL variant; do not open a second architecture.

model_rtl_drift_p0: Reusing row_complete == scratch_write_enable silently drops dead-row architectural completions
Leaving M474/M498 separate read and write outputs unconstrained silently restores concurrent-1R1W and the 389974420-cycle ceiling
Computing live metadata after execution starts, storing one non-ping-pong copy, or treating it as a free oracle invalidates task overlap and capacity
Adding single-use store elision implements combined PVRF, which is outside the only authorized candidate
Changing popcount/row-ID order, equal-later exclusion, subset tie policy, one-lookahead rule, or no-consume-credit rule invalidates the M505 schedule
Using one response word cannot reproduce pending-response plus forward dual enqueue; using the old packed two-slot block without a clean physical solution repeats M477/M498
Treating the generated macros as 64x128 rather than 128x128 undercharges capacity by 9216 bytes; omitting any of the nine slices corrupts the 1152-bit row
Assuming combinational or two-cycle SRAM response instead of the generated one-cycle synchronous contract changes stalls and parent readiness
Failing to block a same-address prefetch while final psum output is stalled reintroduces the independently reproduced stale-RAW bug
Comparing CPU cycles with zero-macro M475 area, or hiding the 30.457 GB logical parent movement, produces an invalid DATE efficiency claim
